I couldn't do this research, so I haven't written any notes. My one attempt to load the pages failed: the tool reported that I'd used up my allowed web calls for this turn. No pages loaded, so nothing was retrieved from Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Ellicott, Pulpit, Gill, Barnes), Precept Austin or any other site.

You asked me to report only what the sources say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I have no source material, writing verse-by-verse notes now would break that rule, so there are no notes below. That includes the Protestant differences and the other views.

**Next turn I would:**
1. **Traditional reading (vv. 1–13):** read Enduring Word, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Gill on Isaiah 46, plus Precept Austin's Isaiah 46 page.
2. **Where Protestants differ:** the likely place is vv. 10–11 ("My purpose will stand… I will accomplish"). I'd check Reformed sources on God's decree and foreknowledge (Ligonier, Monergism, Desiring God) against Wesleyan/Methodist ones (Wesley's notes at wesley.nnu.edu, Seedbed). I'd also look for how sources read the "bird of prey from the east" (traditionally Cyrus) and "My righteousness" in v. 13.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship on Bel/Nebo and the date of the text; New Advent, catholic.com and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings. I'd include popular modern teaching only if those sites actually discuss it.

If you reply "continue," I'll start fetching and send the notes in the format you asked for, with a URL after every point.
